question: An electric bulb draws a current of 0.15 { A} for 8 minutes. How much electric charge flows through the circuit during this time?
solution:
The correct answer is __**72 C**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The relationship between **electric current**, **electric charge**, and **time** is governed by the fundamental formula **Q = I × t**, where **Q** represents the **total charge** in **Coulombs (C)**, **I** represents the **current** in **Amperes (A)**, and **t** represents the **time** in **seconds (s)**.
 
• In this specific numerical problem, the **electric current (I)** drawn by the bulb is given as **0.15 A**. *Hence, the identification of current is correct.*
 
• The **time (t)** for which the current flows is provided as **8 minutes**. Since the **SI unit** for time in this equation must be **seconds**, we perform the conversion: **8 minutes × 60 seconds/minute = 480 seconds**. *Hence, the time conversion is correct.*
 
• By substituting these values into the formula, we calculate the charge: **Q = 0.15 A × 480 s**. This multiplication results in a **numerical value** of **72**. *Hence, the mathematical calculation is correct.*
 
• The **SI unit** of **electric charge** is the **Coulomb (C)**. Therefore, the total charge flowing through the circuit is **72 C**. *Hence, the final derivation of the answer is correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Electric Current:**

 
 
• **Electric current** is defined as the **rate of flow** of electric charges across a cross-section of a conductor. It is a **scalar quantity** even though it has a direction.
 
• The **SI unit** of current is the **Ampere (A)**, named after the **French scientist Andre-Marie Ampere** in the **year 1820**.
 
• **1 Ampere** is constituted by the flow of **1 Coulomb** of charge per **second**.
 
 
 
• **Electric Charge (Q):**
 
 
• The **Coulomb (C)** is the **SI unit** of charge. It is equivalent to the charge contained in nearly **6 × 10^18 electrons**.
 
• The charge of a **single electron** is approximately **1.6 × 10^-19 C**.
 
• Charges are of two types: **positive** (protons) and **negative** (electrons). In a metallic wire, the flow of **electrons** constitutes the current.
 
 
 
• **Measuring Instruments:**
 
 
• An **Ammeter** is a device used to measure **electric current** in a circuit. To ensure **accurate measurement**, it is always connected in **series** because it has **very low internal resistance**.
 
• A **Voltmeter** is used to measure **potential difference** and is connected in **parallel** across the points where the measurement is needed.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Direction of Current:** Conventionally, the direction of **electric current** is taken as opposite to the direction of the flow of **electrons** (which are **negative charges**). It flows from the **positive terminal** to the **negative terminal** of a cell or battery.
 
• **Safety and Circuits:** The **electric bulb** in the question acts as a **resistor**. The **amount of charge** flowing determines the **energy consumed** over time.
 
• **Common Conversions:** In **physics problems**, time is often given in **minutes** or **hours**, but for **Standard units**, it must always be converted to **seconds** before using the **Q = It** formula. For example, **1 hour** equals **3600 seconds**.
 
• **Application of Charge:** The concept of **electric charge** is fundamental in **electrostatics** and **electrodynamics**, used in **applications** ranging from **household appliances** to large-scale **industrial machinery**.
